title: vauquelinia corymbosa subsp. angustifolia
intro: Vauquelinia corymbosa subsp. angustifolia, commonly known as "Mexican buckthorn," is a plant species native to the southwestern regions of North America. The plant is used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include its ability to treat various gastrointestinal issues, such as diarrhea, and its potential anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Vauquelinia corymbosa subsp. angustifolia include its use as an emetic and purgative, and its potential anti-diarrheal and anti-inflammatory effects. The bioactive constituents of this plant include saponins, flavonoids, and alkaloids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
